subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 2: Climate Change – Listening and Speaking: Debate
outcomes: Understand debate words like policy, emission, consumer and eco-friendly.
Listen to a debate and sort arguments into for and against.
Take part in a debate using polite debate expressions.

tf.s: A consumer is a person who buys goods or services.
tf.why: Yes! When you buy something, you are a consumer.

tf.s: A policy is a set of ideas officially agreed by a government.
The topic of the debate in Listening 2.3 is that governments are responsible for stopping global warming.
tf.why: Well done, you found the topic.

tf.s: 'Governments can regulate factories' is an argument against the debate topic.
tf.why: It supports the topic, so it is an argument for.

tf.s: 'You are right to some extent, but…' shows partial agreement.
tf.why: Right, you agree a little but add a different idea.

tf.s: 'To sum up…' is used to start a debate.
tf.why: 'To sum up' is used to finish and summarise.

tf.s: In a debate, we stress important words to make our point stronger.
tf.why: Yes, e.g. GOVERNMENTS should REGULATE factories.

tf.s: 'Switch off' means to start a machine.
tf.why: 'Switch off' means to stop a machine.

tf.s: An eco-friendly product harms the environment.
tf.why: Eco-friendly means not harmful to the environment.

boxes.why: 'We believe that…' presents your team's view.

boxes.q: I see your ___, but I disagree.
boxes.why: 'I see your point' politely accepts an idea before disagreeing.

boxes.q: Which phrasal verb means 'stop a machine'?
boxes.why: Switch off the TV when you leave the room.

boxes.q: ___ up your water bottle instead of buying a new one.
Which expression shows you disagree politely?
boxes.why: It disagrees in a polite way.

boxes.q: Which word describes a bag that does not harm nature?
boxes.why: Eco-friendly things are good for the environment.

boxes.q: Which is an idea to reduce your carbon footprint?
Which phrasal verb means 'learn or discover information'?
boxes.why: We find out facts by researching.

hunt.q: A formal discussion: for and against

mcq.q: What is the topic of the debate in Listening 2.3?
o: Governments are responsible for stopping global warming.
mcq.why: The speakers argue about governments' responsibility.

o: You are right to some extent, but…
mcq.why: It agrees a little and then adds a 'but'.

mcq.q: Which expression ends a debate argument?
mcq.why: 'To sum up' gives a short summary at the end.

mcq.q: Which words should we stress in 'Governments should regulate emissions'?
mcq.why: We stress the key information words.

mcq.q: Choose an argument AGAINST 'It is easy to live a more eco-friendly lifestyle'.
o: We can turn off the lights.
We can fill up a water bottle.
mcq.why: High prices make it harder, so this is against.

mcq.q: Your opponent makes a strong argument. You agree with it. What do you say?
Is 'Governments can regulate factories' for or against the debate topic?
o: for, because it shows governments can act
against, because it is about money
mcq.why: It supports the idea that governments are responsible.

mcq.q: Which argument is supported with a reason and an example?
o: I disagree because people also have a responsibility. For example, we can reduce plastic use.
mcq.why: A strong argument gives a reason and an example.

mcq.q: Why is stressing important words useful in a debate?
o: It makes the main points clear and strong.
It means you don't need reasons.
